name: Hashabiah
overview: Hashabiah was a male Levite, specifically a descendant of the Merarite clan through Mushi, son of Merari, who was one of Levi's sons. He is noted as the son of Amaziah and served as a Levite during the time of the return from exile, reflecting his role within the post-exilic community. His lineage situates him within the priestly and temple service traditions of ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabiah means 'YHWH has reckoned,' indicating a recognition of God's sovereign accounting or judgment. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:45, reflects a theologically significant meaning tied to the divine name YHWH, though it was not indicated to be given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hashabiah as the son of Amaziah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 6:45. There is also an inferred relationship to Malluch as his father, based on the same verse. Beyond these connections, no additional family relationships are documented in the provided records.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabiah's importance lies in his role as a Levite during the return from exile, a critical period for reestablishing worship and temple service in Israel. His descent from the Merarite clan highlights the continuity of Levitical duties passed down through generations, emphasizing the restoration of proper religious order under God's providence. His presence in the genealogical records underscores the faithfulness of God's people in preserving their heritage and serving Him after the Babylonian captivity.
